classification.difficultyReason: Requires generalising the scaffolded tree counts to 2^n outcomes and recognising that excluding the single all-tail path counts every outcome with at least one head. The earlier numerical cases support, but do not supply, this symbolic generalisation.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A coin is tossed twice. By drawing a tree diagram, calculate the probability that at least one head is obtained.

answer.worked:
H means head and T means tail. The tree gives four equally likely outcomes: HH, HT, TH and TT. Three contain at least one head.

$$P(\text{at least one head})=\frac{3}{4}.$$

spec.description: Complete two-stage coin tree, following the left-to-right taught tree convention.
spec.mathematics: Two branches at each toss; terminal outcomes HH, HT, TH, TT.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A coin is tossed three times. By drawing a tree diagram, calculate the probability that at least one head is obtained.

answer.worked:
The tree gives eight equally likely outcomes: HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH and TTT. Only TTT has no head, so seven outcomes contain at least one head.

$$P(\text{at least one head})=\frac{7}{8}.$$

spec.description: Complete three-stage coin tree with all eight terminal sequences.
spec.mathematics: Two branches per stage; seven terminal sequences contain H, and only TTT does not.

children.label: c
children.prompt: A coin is tossed four times.

children.label: i
children.prompt: How many outcomes are there? (Hint: Try to picture what the tree diagram would look like without actually drawing it.)

answer.worked:
Each toss doubles the number of paths in the tree.

$$\text{Number of outcomes}=2\times2\times2\times2=16.$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: What is the probability that at least one head is obtained?

answer.worked:
Of the 16 equally likely outcomes, only TTTT has no head. Therefore 15 outcomes contain at least one head.

$$P(\text{at least one head})=\frac{16-1}{16}=\frac{15}{16}.$$

There are two possible results at each of the $n$ stages, so the number of terminal paths doubles at each stage.

$$\text{Number of outcomes}=2^n.$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: What is the probability that at least one head is obtained?

answer.short:
$\frac{2^n-1}{2^n}$

Exclude the single outcome consisting entirely of tails.
answer.worked:
There are $2^n$ equally likely outcomes. Exactly one has no heads: tails on every toss. Thus $2^n-1$ outcomes contain at least one head.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one head})&=\frac{2^n-1}{2^n}\\P(\text{at least one head})&=1-\frac{1}{2^n}.\end{align*}$$
